I need to summarize what Argus actually did here in plain terms — it filed a record of what was tried during the incident, including reverting the monthly-spend feature, and the postmortem notes the bug is still present in the code with a PR left in draft awaiting human review.

The alert came in at 12:08:02, and investigation traced it to the monthly-spend-feature flag being turned on at 12:02, which triggered a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py:47, spiking the error rate from ~1% to 30-35%. No deploy was involved — Argus just flipped the flag back off at 12:08:04, confirmed by 12:10:03 that the service had returned to normal since 12:08, and marked the incident mitigated. It drafted PR #360 and wrote up the postmortem, but left it unmerged since turning the flag back on would just reintroduce the same failure.

input.answer:
Argus picked up the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop at 12:08:02 UTC. Its investigation found that the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 12:02. The new spend summary code then raised a ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate went from about 1% to 30–35%. No deploy was recorded.

At 12:08:04 Argus switched that flag from ON to OFF. By 12:10:03 it had confirmed the service was back to normal from 12:08, and moved the incident to MITIGATED. The alert that fired has stopped firing.

It also opened a draft fix, PR #360 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/360), which a person needs to review and merge. It logged the flag revert in its record of what was tried and wrote a postmortem. The postmortem estimates the shop took 4,006.73 USD less than in the same hours on earlier weeks.

The bad division is still in the code. Turning monthly-spend-feature back on before the fix is merged would likely break account pages again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
